items.title: Tired of Being Put on Hold? Transfer Your Prescription to Us in 2 Minutes — No Phone Calls Needed
items.summary: Switching pharmacies is easier than most patients realize. At Fenkell Rx Pharmacy, we handle the entire transfer for you — you never have to call your old pharmacy. Here is exactly how it works.
items.body:
If you have ever waited 20 minutes on hold just to request a refill, been dismissed at the counter, or felt like a number instead of a patient — you are not alone. We hear this from new patients every week. The good news is that switching pharmacies takes about two minutes and you do not have to make a single phone call to your old pharmacy.

How prescription transfers work at Fenkell Rx

When you request a transfer to Fenkell Rx Pharmacy, we do all the work. You give us your name, date of birth, the medication name, and the name and phone number of your current pharmacy. We call them, request the transfer, and notify you when it is ready. Most transfers are completed same day.

You can start a transfer three ways: fill out the form at fenkellrxpharmacy.com/transfer, call us at (313) 519-5700, or walk in to 18360 Fenkell Ave, Detroit MI 48223. There is no fee. There is no paperwork on your end.

Can I transfer a controlled substance?

Partial transfers are allowed for controlled substances in Michigan — whatever remaining refills are on your prescription can be transferred. For Schedule II controlled substances (like Adderall or certain pain medications), a new prescription from your doctor is required rather than a transfer. Call us and we can walk you through the specifics for your medication.

Will my insurance still work after I transfer?

Yes. Your copay and coverage stay exactly the same — we are in-network with Medicare Part D, Medicaid, Blue Cross Blue Shield, United Healthcare, Aetna, Cigna, Humana, and most major plans. Your insurance follows your prescription, not your old pharmacy.

What happens to my refill history?

Your remaining refills transfer with the prescription. If you had 3 refills left at your old pharmacy, you will have 3 refills left here. Nothing is lost.

Why patients switch to Fenkell Rx

We are an independently owned pharmacy, which means the pharmacist who fills your prescription is also the one who answers the phone. There are no corporate scripts, no 45-minute hold queues, and no telling patients a medication is unavailable without actually trying to source it. We stock medications that major chains routinely run out of, and we offer free same-day delivery so you do not have to leave home if you cannot.

If you have been putting off switching because you thought it would be complicated — it is not. Start at fenkellrxpharmacy.com/transfer or call (313) 519-5700.

items.title: See a Doctor Online Today and Pick Up Your Prescription Same Day in Detroit
items.summary: Through our QuickCare service, Detroit-area patients can book an online doctor visit, get a diagnosis, and have their prescription filled and ready for pickup or same-day delivery — all without leaving home for the appointment.
items.body:
Getting sick on a Tuesday should not mean waiting three weeks for a doctor's appointment or spending four hours in an urgent care waiting room. Through Fenkell Rx Pharmacy's QuickCare service, you can see a licensed doctor online in minutes, get a prescription, and have it filled the same day — either for pickup at our Fenkell Ave location or delivered free to your door.

What is an online doctor visit?

An online doctor visit (also called a telehealth visit) connects you with a licensed physician through a video or text-based appointment on your phone or computer. The doctor reviews your symptoms, asks questions, and if appropriate, sends a prescription directly to a pharmacy. Through QuickCare, that pharmacy is us — so your prescription is already being filled while you finish the appointment.

What conditions can be treated?

Online visits work well for a wide range of common conditions including sinus infections, urinary tract infections (UTIs), cold and flu symptoms, allergies, skin rashes, ear infections, pink eye, migraines, and more. If the doctor determines your condition needs an in-person evaluation, they will tell you — but most routine illnesses can be handled entirely online.

How fast is the process?

Most patients complete their online visit within 15 to 30 minutes. Once the doctor sends the prescription to Fenkell Rx Pharmacy, we typically have it ready within one to two hours. If you need it delivered, our free same-day delivery covers Northwest Detroit, Redford Township, and Southfield.

Does insurance cover the online visit?

Many insurance plans now cover telehealth at the same rate as in-person visits, particularly since 2020. The prescription itself is billed through your normal pharmacy insurance — your copay is the same as any other prescription. We recommend checking your specific plan for the telehealth visit cost.

How do I get started?

Visit fenkellrxpharmacy.com/quickcare to book your online visit. If you have questions beforehand, call us at (313) 519-5700. We are located at 18360 Fenkell Ave, Detroit, MI 48223 for pickup, or we can deliver free to your address.

items.title: Refill Your Prescriptions Online in Detroit — No Hold Times, No Lines, Free Delivery
items.summary: Detroit-area patients can request prescription refills online at any time through Fenkell Rx Pharmacy. We fill same day and deliver free across Northwest Detroit, Redford Township, and Southfield — so you never have to wait in a pharmacy line again.
items.body:
Prescription refills should not require a 30-minute hold, a trip across town, or a half-day waiting at a pharmacy counter. At Fenkell Rx Pharmacy, you can request your refill online in under two minutes — and we will have it ready for same-day pickup or deliver it free to your door.

How to refill online

Go to fenkellrxpharmacy.com/refills and fill out the short form: your name, date of birth, Rx number (found on your medication bottle), and your preferred pickup or delivery method. That is it. We receive the request instantly and get to work. You will hear from us when it is ready.

What if I do not have my Rx number?

Call us at (313) 519-5700 and we can look up your prescription by name and date of birth. If your prescription has already transferred to us from a previous pharmacy, we can find it in our system right away.

How long does a refill take?

Most refills submitted before 3:00 PM are ready same day. We will text or call you when your prescription is ready. If you need delivery, our free same-day service covers Northwest Detroit, Redford Township, and Southfield — no minimum order, no delivery fee.

What medications can be refilled online?

Most maintenance medications — blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid, cholesterol, mental health, and others — can be refilled online as long as your prescription has active refills remaining. Controlled substances require an in-person prescription from your doctor under Michigan law, but we can help you coordinate that process.

Does insurance apply to online refills?

Yes. Online refills go through your insurance the same way as walk-in refills. We accept Medicare Part D, Medicaid, Blue Cross Blue Shield, United Healthcare, Aetna, Cigna, Humana, Molina, and most major plans. Your copay is unchanged.

Why refill at Fenkell Rx?

We are an independent pharmacy, which means a real pharmacist reviews every prescription we fill. If there is a question about your medication, a possible interaction, or a dosing concern, we call you directly — not a call center, not an automated message. We stock medications that major chains regularly run short on, and if we do not have something, we will tell you honestly and source it as quickly as possible. Start your refill at fenkellrxpharmacy.com/refills or call (313) 519-5700.

items.title: Medicare Now Covers Weight Loss Drugs for $50/Month - The New GLP-1 Bridge Program Explained
items.summary: As of July 1, 2026, eligible Medicare Part D members can get Wegovy, Zepbound (KwikPen), or Foundayo for a flat $50 monthly copay under the new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program. Most patients (and many chain pharmacy counters) do not know about it yet. Here is how it works and how our Detroit pharmacists can help.
items.body:
Starting July 1, 2026, Medicare is covering GLP-1 weight loss medications for the first time through a temporary federal program called the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge. If you or a family member is on Medicare and has been told these medications are not covered, that answer just changed - and many pharmacy counters have not caught up yet.

## What the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge covers

The program provides eligible Medicare Part D members access to specific GLP-1 medications approved for weight loss at a flat $50 copay for each 30-day supply. The covered medications are Wegovy (both injection and tablet forms), Zepbound (KwikPen form only - single-dose vials and pens are not covered), and Foundayo. The program runs from July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027.

## Who qualifies

You must be enrolled in a Medicare Part D prescription drug plan or a Medicare Advantage plan that includes drug coverage. Eligibility is based on body mass index (BMI) and health status: generally a BMI of 35 or higher, or a BMI of 30 to 34.9 along with a qualifying condition such as uncontrolled high blood pressure or certain forms of heart failure. Your doctor must submit a prior authorization request through the CMS central processor before the prescription can be filled under the program.

## Important fine print

The $50 copay is the same in every Part D phase, but because the Bridge operates outside of the normal Part D benefit, the copay does not count toward your Part D deductible or annual out-of-pocket maximum, and Extra Help (the Low-Income Subsidy) does not reduce it. If you already receive a GLP-1 through your Part D plan for a covered condition like type 2 diabetes, you are not eligible for the Bridge - you simply continue your existing coverage.

## How our pharmacists can help

This is a brand-new program and the paperwork is unfamiliar to a lot of prescriber offices and big-chain pharmacy counters. As an independent pharmacy, we take the time to walk you through it: we can check whether your Part D plan qualifies, explain what your doctor needs to submit for prior authorization, and coordinate with your prescriber so your prescription is ready to fill once approval comes through. Ask your doctor to send your prescription to Fenkell Rx Pharmacy, 18360 Fenkell Ave, Detroit, MI 48223 - or call us at (313) 519-5700 and we will help you get started.

A valid prescription and program prior authorization are required. Eligibility is determined by CMS program rules, not by the pharmacy. This article is general information, not medical or insurance advice - talk to your doctor about whether a GLP-1 medication is right for you.
